Registered Auditors · Zuidplein 140, 1077 XV Amsterdam, Netherlands · Independent Auditor to the Borrower
AUDIT FILE REF ACC-7604/FY2025
Notes to the Financial Statements
Altai Metals Holding B.V. · Year ended 31 December 2025
These notes accompany the management accounts for the financial year 2025 and should be read
together with the loan covenant schedule. Amounts are stated in US dollars unless otherwise noted.
Note 1 — Basis of Preparation
These financial statements present the accounts of Altai Metals Holding B.V. and have been prepared
in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards as issued by the International
Accounting Standards Board. They are prepared on the historical cost basis, except for those financial
instruments that are measured at fair value, and on a going-concern basis, the directors having a
reasonable expectation that the Company has adequate resources to continue in operational existence
for the foreseeable future. The accounting policies set out below have been applied consistently to all
periods presented.
Note 2 — Significant Accounting Policies
The preparation of these statements requires the consistent application of recognition and
measurement policies across reporting periods. Where a new or amended Standard has become
effective during the year, its adoption has not had a material effect on the amounts reported.
Comparative information has been reclassified where necessary to conform with the presentation
adopted in the current year, and such reclassification does not affect previously reported results or
equity.
Note 3 — Revenue Recognition
Revenue is recognised in accordance with IFRS 15, Revenue from Contracts with Customers, when
control of the promised goods or services transfers to the customer, in an amount that reflects the
consideration to which the Company expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services.
The Company identifies the performance obligations in each contract, allocates the transaction price to
those obligations, and recognises revenue as each obligation is satisfied, either over time or at a point
in time, according to the substance of the arrangement.
Note 4 — Property, Plant and Equipment
Items of property, plant and equipment are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation and any
accumulated impairment losses. Depreciation is charged to profit or loss on a straight-line basis over
the estimated useful lives of each component, which are reviewed at each reporting date and adjusted
prospectively if expectations differ from previous estimates. The carrying amount of an asset is written

disposal are determined by comparing proceeds with carrying amount.
Note 5 — Foreign Currency Translation
Transactions denominated in currencies other than the functional currency are recorded at the
exchange rates prevailing at the dates of the transactions. Monetary assets and liabilities so
denominated are retranslated at the closing rate at the reporting date, and the resulting exchange
differences are recognised in profit or loss. Non-monetary items measured at historical cost are not
retranslated. The rates applied in the ordinary course of preparation are those published by the
National Bank for the relevant settlement dates.
Note 6 — Related Party Transactions
In the ordinary course of business the Company enters into transactions with related parties, including
entities under common control and key management personnel, which are disclosed in accordance
with IAS 24, Related Party Disclosures. Such transactions are conducted on terms that the directors
consider to be equivalent to those prevailing in arm's-length dealings, and outstanding balances at the
reporting date are unsecured and settled in cash. No guarantees have been given or received in respect
of these balances.
Note 7 — Financial Instruments and Risk Management
Financial assets and liabilities are recognised when the Company becomes a party to the contractual
provisions of the instrument and are classified and measured in accordance with IFRS 9. The
Company is exposed to credit risk, liquidity risk and market risk in the normal course of its activities.
Credit risk is managed through counterparty assessment and the monitoring of receivable ageing;
liquidity risk is managed by maintaining adequate banking facilities and by forecasting cash
requirements; and market risk is managed by monitoring exposure to movements in interest rates and
exchange rates.
COVENANT COMPLIANCE ADDENDUM
The following disclosures supplement the notes above and are prepared by the auditor solely for
covenant-testing purposes under the Credit Agreement.
Note 8 — Foreign Exchange
The foreign-exchange conversion applied for covenant-testing purposes was examined in the course of
the procedures. The determinations on this matter are set out in report on agreed-upon review
procedures No. AR-2025-0106 and are not repeated here.
No reclassifications were required for the covenant period.
